title: Design an Instant Messaging System (WhatsApp)
subtitle: Sticky WebSocket gateways, delivery receipts, offline queue & group fan-out
functionalReqs: 1-on-1 real-time chat with <100ms delivery when online.
Message delivery receipts: Sent (✓), Delivered (✓✓), Read (blue ✓✓).
Offline message queuing and reliable sync upon reconnection.
Group chats up to 500–1,000 members + online/last-seen presence.

nonFunctionalReqs.rationale: Each active mobile/web client holds an open bidirectional socket.
Replies must never appear out of causal sequence inside a conversation.

nonFunctionalReqs.target: Zero lost messages once Sent ✓ acked
nonFunctionalReqs.rationale: Users treat chat history as guaranteed reliable delivery.

workedSummary.websocketFleet: 100M concurrent sockets ÷ 100k sockets/node ≈ 1,000 stateful Chat Gateways
workedSummary.dailyTextStorage: 20B × 250 B ≈ 5 TB/day (offload server retention once delivered if ephemeral, or retain in wide-column store)

coreEntities.name: ChatMessage
coreEntities.storageEngine: Cassandra / ScyllaDB (LSM-tree optimized for high write throughput)

apiContracts.purpose: Persistent bidirectional frame channel for send_msg, ack_delivered, ack_read, heartbeat
Catch-up sync for multi-device or offline reconnect

explorerTopology.title: 1-on-1 & Offline Chat Delivery Flow
explorerTopology.subtitle: Stateful WebSocket gateway routing via Redis session map + Cassandra LSM storage
explorerTopology.overview: Unlike stateless REST APIs, chat servers maintain millions of persistent WebSocket connections. A shared Redis Session Registry maps `user_id -> gateway_host` so Gateway A can route messages directly to Bob's Gateway B (or store in Cassandra + trigger APNs/FCM push if Bob is offline).
keyTakeaways: Partition Cassandra messages by `chat_id` clustered by monotonic `message_id` (Snowflake/HLC) so chat history scans are single-partition sequential reads.
Use `client_msg_id` deduplication so flaky cellular retries don't send duplicate texts.
Separate Presence heartbeats with debouncing/TTL so flaky connections don't cause online/offline UI flicker.

nodes.label: Alice Mobile
nodes.summary: Sender maintaining persistent WebSocket to Chat Gateway A.
failureModes: Cellular handoff drops socket silently unless ping/pong keepalives detect half-open TCP

nodes.label: Chat Gateway A
nodes.summary: Holds Alice's TCP socket, assigns monotonic server sequence, persists message, and forwards to Bob's gateway.
failureModes: Thundering herd reconnect storm if a gateway crashes—clients must use exponential jitter!

nodes.label: Session & Presence Map
nodes.summary: Tracks which Chat Gateway currently holds each online user's socket.
failureModes: Stale pointer if gateway dies abruptly without deleting keys (mitigated by 30s TTL)

nodes.label: Cassandra Message Store
nodes.summary: High-write LSM store holding persisted chat messages & offline inbox queue.
failureModes: Unbounded partition growth on multi-year active chats (solve with monthly bucket suffix)

nodes.label: Chat Gateway B
nodes.summary: Receives internal gRPC forward from Gateway A and pushes immediately down Bob's open WebSocket.
failureModes: Bob disconnects mid-flight -> fallback immediately to Push Notification + Offline DB

nodes.label: Bob Mobile
nodes.summary: Recipient client sending back Delivered ✓✓ and Read blue ✓✓ acks.
failureModes: Multi-device sync requires tracking per-device watermarks

steps.info: Alice sends encrypted frame (clientMsgId=m_991) -> Gateway A assigns Snowflake msgId
steps.inspectorNote: Server checks clientMsgId idempotency cache to guarantee retries never duplicate messages.

steps.info: Persisted to Cassandra quorum -> Alice receives Sent (✓) ack
steps.payloadInspector: INSERT INTO messages (chat_id, msg_id, body) IF NOT EXISTS -> QUORUM ACK
steps.inspectorNote: Only after durable write succeeds does Alice see the single Sent checkmark.

steps.payloadInspector: Bob active on Gateway B (last heartbeat 4s ago)
steps.inspectorNote: If Bob were offline (`nil`), Gateway A enqueues an APNs/FCM push notification and marks message pending sync.

steps.info: Gateway B pushes frame to Bob -> Bob acks Delivered (✓✓) back to Alice
steps.payloadInspector: Bob device receives ciphertext -> emits {op:"ack_delivered", msgId:"..."}
steps.inspectorNote: Total end-to-end online delivery stays ~27ms plus last-mile RTT.

chaosScenarios.title: Gateway B Crash (100k Socket Drop + Offline Fallback)
chaosScenarios.triggerSummary: Chat Gateway B crashes abruptly, dropping 100,000 active user WebSockets including Bob's.
chaosScenarios.mitigationSummary: Gateway A's gRPC forward fails -> falls back to APNs/FCM push notification while message stays safe in Cassandra; clients reconnect with randomized backoff jitter so login/session services don't melt.

steps.info: Connection refused on Gateway B -> message already durable in Cassandra; trigger FCM/APNs wake push
steps.payloadInspector: gRPC UNAVAILABLE -> delete stale Redis session:bob -> enqueue APNs wake alert
steps.inspectorNote: Because step 2 persisted the message before routing, zero messages are lost during a gateway crash.

steps.info: Bob reconnects with random jitter (1–15s) to healthy Gateway A & pulls messages > lastAckedId
steps.inspectorNote: Exponential backoff + full jitter prevents 100k simultaneous TLS handshakes from crashing surviving gateways.

pros: Compact framing overhead for typing indicators & receipts
cons: Requires connection registry (Redis) + careful draining during deploys
tradeoffs.bestFor: Real-time chat, multiplayer collaboration, live trading

cons: Higher header/reconnect overhead on frequent bidirectional chat
tradeoffs.bestFor: Unidirectional feeds or LLM token streaming (SSE)

deepDives.title: Group Chat Fan-Out Scaling
deepDives.bottleneck: Broadcasting to 500-member groups synchronously blocks sender gateways.
deepDives.solution: Cap small-group fan-out via async Kafka Message Router looking up member session pointers in batches; for massive channels (>5k users), switch to pull-based inbox/channel feeds.
deepDives.tradeoff: Increases latency slightly for large groups while keeping 1-on-1 chat fast.

deepDives.title: Causal Message Ordering Across Devices
deepDives.bottleneck: Client device clocks drift wildly (wrong timestamps).
deepDives.solution: Assign server-side per-chat monotonic sequence numbers or Snowflake/Hybrid Logical Clock IDs inside the chat partition.
deepDives.tradeoff: Requires routing chat writes consistently or ordering by server arrival time.

criteria: Uses Redis session map across gateways
Explains Sent/Delivered/Read flow + offline push fallback
Handles reconnect storm jitter & group fan-out
